subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Two-point perspective uses how many vanishing points?
questions.explain: Two-point perspective uses two vanishing points on the horizon, typically for objects seen at a corner.

questions.q: Screen printing pushes ink through what?
questions.explain: Screen printing forces ink through a fine mesh, with a stencil blocking areas that stay unprinted.

questions.q: Lino printing is an example of which type of printmaking?
questions.explain: In relief printing such as lino, ink sits on the raised surface while cut-away areas stay blank.

questions.q: What is the secondary colour made by mixing red and yellow?
questions.explain: Red mixed with yellow produces the secondary colour orange.

questions.q: Which drawing medium is best for soft, smudgeable, very dark marks?
questions.explain: Charcoal produces rich, dark, easily smudged marks ideal for tonal drawing.

questions.q: What is the key difference between shape and form?
options: Shape is two-dimensional, form is three-dimensional
Shape is coloured, form is not
Shape is large, form is small
questions.explain: A shape is flat and two-dimensional, while a form has depth and appears three-dimensional.

questions.q: Collage is an artwork made by...
options: Sticking different materials onto a surface
questions.explain: Collage assembles and glues various materials, such as paper or fabric, onto a surface.

options: A thin, transparent layer of diluted paint
Thick paint applied with a knife
questions.explain: A wash is a thin, transparent layer of watercolour spread over an area to build colour gradually.

questions.q: In a composition, what is the 'focal point'?
options: The main area that draws the viewer's eye
The darkest area of the picture
questions.explain: The focal point is the part of the composition that attracts the viewer's attention first.
The 'B' scale denotes softer, darker pencils, so 6B is much softer and darker than an H grade.

questions.q: Which medium is a soft, powdery stick available in soft (chalk) or oil form?
questions.explain: Pastels are sticks of pigment, made as soft chalk pastels or richer oil pastels.

questions.q: In a mono-print, how many prints can usually be taken from one inking?
questions.explain: A mono-print produces a single, unique image, unlike editions made from a fixed block or plate.
